newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's opposition welcomes offer to debate law.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's opposition welcomes offer to debate law.

text.p: South Korea's main opposition leader said on Tuesday he welcomed an offer by President Kim Young-sam to reexamine a controversial new labour law with opposition parties.

Kim Dae-jung, head of the National Congress for New Politics, also told a news conference the president had given an assurance that force would not be used to arrest strike leaders and the government would not seek to renew arrest warrants once they had expired.
Kim Dae-jung also said the president had agreed to revise another controversial bill that boosts the power of the domestic spy agency.
He said during a lunch meeting at the presidential Blue House he had complained that the security law would intimidate intellectuals, journalists, farmers, workers and opposition politicians.
The president had replied "then revise the national security law too", according to Kim Dae-jung, who added "I was very surprised at this".

"Today's meeting was not a total solution but there was some advance and President Kim Young-sam showed an attitude of wanting to solve the problems together with opposition parties," Kim Dae-jung said.
